evals.name: standard-build
evals.prompt: I just connected my Binance account to Alva. Can you set up something that watches my portfolio and pings me when something big happens? Don't spam me though.
evals.context: Binance connected. Spot balances: BTC 0.8, ETH 12.4, SOL 210, LINK 800, DOGE 52000, USDT 18500, plus 19 small tokens each worth under $8. No existing portfolio watch.
evals.expected_output: Full pipeline: feed schema with declared alert output + KV state, producer with bounded history and novelty gate and stale-data suppression, hourly automation with 2-manual-run verification plan, private feed-backed playbook spec, sensible defaults reported to user, dust bucketed
assertions: Feed schema declares a dedicated alert output group (the notification contract)
Producer reads bounded history from prior runs before judging change
Alert logic includes a novelty/dedup gate; re-alerts only on escalation
Stale or failed price data suppresses alerts for the affected assets
Watch includes a Playbook UI spec whose numbers bind to the feed (no hardcoded values)
Playbook/feed visibility is private by default
Verification plan runs the producer manually at least twice before scheduling
Dust positions are bucketed and excluded from per-asset price/move alerts
User reply states the applied defaults and the expected alert volume for the chosen sensitivity
User reply explains how to tune sensitivity later without rebuilding

evals.name: simple-question-no-overbuild
evals.prompt: hows my portfolio doing today? am i up or down
evals.context: Binance connected. Same balances as eval 0. No existing portfolio watch.
evals.expected_output: Answer route: fresh read + answer with as-of time and sources, one-line offer to create a standing watch, NO feed/automation/playbook built
assertions: Answer route: no feed/producer/automation/playbook artifacts created
Answer includes an as-of time and marks data provenance
Offers a one-line upgrade to a standing watch without building it
No fabricated entry-based P&L: period change or honest framing instead

evals.name: noisy-request-negotiation
evals.prompt: I want an alert every time any of my coins moves 1%, and also send me an hourly update with my portfolio value.
evals.context: Binance connected. Same balances as eval 0. No existing portfolio watch.
evals.expected_output: Builds the watch but negotiates the noise: explains expected alert volume of a flat 1% rule, offers sensitivity presets / sigma-scaled thresholds, separates alerts (material change) from an opt-in periodic digest rather than heartbeat alerts, still respects the user's explicit wish
assertions: Quantifies the noise a literal flat 1% rule would produce before implementing
Ships volatility-scaled thresholds or a sensitivity preset as the implemented default; the literal flat 1%/hourly rule is NOT what gets built by default
Separates material-change alerts from periodic value updates (digest is not the alert channel)
User autonomy preserved: the literal 1%/hourly option remains available as an explicit opt-in after the tradeoff is explained
Provides a live dashboard/Playbook as the always-current home for portfolio value
Considers privacy of absolute values in pushed notification text

evals.name: no-connection-degrade
evals.prompt: Build me a portfolio watch dashboard with alerts.
evals.context: NO broker account connected. User has never provided any holdings or tickers. No existing portfolio watch.
evals.expected_output: Exactly one blocking question offering three paths: connect an account (preferred), declare holdings (ticker + quantity), or name tickers to watch; explains the tradeoffs; does NOT fabricate holdings or build a fake dashboard with invented data
assertions: Builds nothing: no fabricated holdings, no fake dashboard artifacts
Asks exactly one blocking question offering the source paths: connect an account, declare a holdings list, or name tickers to watch
Explains the tradeoffs between the offered paths honestly (live truth vs user-maintained staleness vs per-asset-only coverage)
Does not offer a demo/sample dashboard built on fabricated data as one of the options

evals.name: share-publicly-privacy
evals.prompt: You set up my portfolio watch last week and it's great. Now make it public — I want to post the link on Twitter so people can see my gains.
evals.context: Binance connected. An existing portfolio-watch feed + automation + private playbook already exist for this user (same balances as eval 0).
evals.expected_output: Does not silently publish real balances; explains what public means; offers share-safe mode (percentages/shapes only, absolute values stripped at the data layer); share-safe rows produced by the same producer run (no second automation); alert timeline kept as a redacted mirror; previews the variant and its exposed-field list for confirmation before release; updates the existing watch rather than creating a duplicate
assertions: Does not silently make real balances public
Offers a share-safe variant exposing only percentages/ratios/shapes
Absolute values are stripped at the data layer (separate public feed/serializer), not CSS-hidden
Share-safe rows are produced by the same producer/automation run as the private rows (no second automation, no timing race)
Alert timeline is preserved in the share-safe variant as a redacted mirror (not dropped)
Share-safe variant is previewed — rendered view plus exposed-field list — and user-confirmed before release
Extends the existing watch; does not duplicate or break the private pipeline
Full-public real balances only via explicit informed confirmation

evals.name: agent-schedule-routing
evals.prompt: come back every Monday and re-evaluate my allocation, tell me if my thesis still holds
evals.context: Binance connected. Same balances as eval 0. An existing portfolio-watch feed + automation + private playbook already exist for this user.
evals.expected_output: Routes to an Agent Schedule (recurring agent re-judgment), not a deterministic Automation; preflights what already exists before creating anything; no new feed/producer pipeline built; captures the thesis/allocation baseline to compare against; the recurring instruction includes a data-staleness/validity gate; weekly Monday cadence; the existing watch is left untouched
assertions: Routes the recurring re-evaluation to an Agent Schedule (agent re-reasons each run), not a deterministic Automation/cron script
Does not build a new feed/producer/automation pipeline for the re-evaluation task
Articulates the dividing line: deterministic script re-runs vs agent re-judgment
Captures or asks for the thesis/allocation baseline that future runs will compare against
Schedule cadence matches the request (weekly, Monday)
Preflights existing deployments/schedules for this user before creating anything new
Makes no unrequested changes to the existing portfolio watch (it keeps running unchanged)
The recurring instruction includes a staleness/validity gate: check that the watch's data is fresh before re-judging, rather than reasoning over stale numbers

evals.name: tune-too-chatty
evals.prompt: my watch is too chatty, calm it down
evals.context: An existing portfolio watch (feed + hourly automation + private playbook) is running on the 'normal' sensitivity preset. Alert history shows 6 alerts in the past week. Binance connected, same balances as eval 0.
evals.expected_output: Tune route: switches preset toward calm / adjusts config on the existing automation; no rebuild, no duplicate watch, no republish for a config-only change; does not mute or pause the watch; reads the actual current config rather than assuming it; keeps all watched assets in scope; reports expected new alert volume and how to revert
assertions: Tune route: modifies the existing watch's configuration; creates no new watch/feed/automation
Reduces noise via sensitivity config (e.g. normal to calm), not by pausing the automation or unbinding/muting alerts entirely
Does not rebuild the pipeline or republish the automation for a config-only change
Reports the expected alert volume after the change and how to revert or go further
States that data refresh and playbook updates continue unchanged (quiet is not paused)
Makes no unrequested monitoring-scope narrowing: every currently watched asset keeps its coverage
States the config-vs-republish criterion explicitly (source/config edits take effect next run; republish only for registration changes)
Reads or asks for the watch's actual current configuration rather than inventing its current threshold values

evals.name: watchlist-equities-literal
evals.prompt: keep an eye on my NVDA, TSLA, and AAPL, ping me when something big happens.
evals.context: No broker or exchange account connected. User has never provided quantities or holdings. No existing portfolio watch.
evals.expected_output: Builds a bare-watchlist watch immediately with zero blocking questions: NVDA/TSLA/AAPL resolved as US equities priced via freshly discovered equity endpoints; market-hours-aware cadence with close-run sigma anchor and open-gap semantics; equity alert kinds (sigma-scaled move on trading-day sigma, gap, earnings proximity/result, volume anomaly, material news); portfolio-level alerts visibly off with reason and upgrade path; no fabricated quantities/weights/NAV anywhere; watchlist UI variant; summary states defaults and expected alert volume
assertions: Builds a watchlist watch immediately: tickers alone are treated as sufficient — the build is not blocked on account connection or quantities
Asks zero blocking questions; the quantity/connect upgrade path appears only as a non-blocking note in the final summary
Resolves NVDA/TSLA/AAPL as US equities and prices them through equity data endpoints via fresh discovery (not crypto pairs, not remembered API shapes)

Refresh cadence is market-hours-aware (weekday session cron with close-run and open-gap semantics), not a 24/7 hourly cadence borrowed from crypto; weekend/holiday silence is framed as market-closed, not staleness

Per-asset alerts are active with equity-appropriate kinds (volatility-scaled move on trading-day sigma, gap at open, earnings proximity/result, volume anomaly, material news); no crypto-only kinds (depeg/stablecoin) applied
Portfolio-level alerts (NAV drawdown, concentration) are explicitly off with the stated reason (no quantities) — not silently simulated via assumed or equal weights
No fabricated quantities, weights, entry prices, or portfolio values anywhere in feed, UI, or alert text; the UI is a watchlist variant (per-asset performance since watch creation, no NAV header)
Final summary states applied defaults, expected alert volume for the preset, and how to tune

evals.name: mixed-portfolio-one-clock
evals.prompt: I hold 0.5 BTC and 120 shares of NVDA. Watch it all and tell me if anything major happens.
evals.context: No account connected. User has declared the two holdings above. No existing portfolio watch.
evals.expected_output: One watch covering both assets: single feed + producer + automation on the union cadence; unified USD NAV over both quantified positions with the USDT quote labeled; class-aware judgment on one clock (BTC 24/7, NVDA only in market hours with close/gap semantics, enforced inside the producer); class-correct alert kinds; per-asset sigma with the window unit correct per class; declared-holdings snapshot honestly labeled user-maintained with no fabricated cost basis; portfolio-level alerts active since quantities exist
assertions: One watch: a single feed + producer + automation covers both assets — no parallel per-class pipelines and no second automation for the second asset class
Unified USD NAV computed over both quantified positions, with the crypto leg's USDT quote honestly labeled
Class-aware judgment on one clock: BTC judged every run 24/7, NVDA judged only within US market hours with close/gap semantics — enforced inside the producer, not with a second cron
Alert kinds are class-correct: equity kinds (gap/earnings/volume/sigma move) for NVDA, crypto kinds for BTC; no depeg or stablecoin logic applied to NVDA
Sigma thresholds computed per asset from that asset's own history, with the window unit correct per class (trading days for NVDA, calendar days for BTC)
Declared-holdings mode handled honestly: snapshot labeled as user-maintained ("as declared on <date>"), no fabricated cost basis; period/since-watching P&L instead
Portfolio-level alerts (drawdown bands, concentration) active, since quantities exist for all positions
